answers.question: check whether the growth is organic and repeatable
answers.answer: Partially supported: the order book rose from ₹39,139 lakhs (FY24) to ₹68,744 lakhs (FY26) and ₹91,655 lakhs by July 2026, which is genuine pipeline rather than one-off revenue [business, page 205]. But 'repeatable' is unproven — margins rose only ~1% while growth consumed cash, and the industry is described as low-barrier and fiercely competitive [business, page 221], so the same growth rate is not bankable.

answers.question: veto — how is the business funded?
answers.answer: Not from its own operations: operating cash flow was negative in all three years and net debt is essentially nil-to-negative, so growth appears funded by equity issuance (net worth tripled to ₹15,678 million, consistent with pre-IPO capital raises) and stretching receivables. The fresh issue vs OFS split could not be read, so whether IPO proceeds fund more of the same is unknown.
